header.userPrompt:
Switch the bank-statement AI category and merchant suggestions from Amazon Nova (Bedrock) to TypeSafe JEV (the "System One" decision model). Keep BOTH the category and merchant suggestions. Keep the existing Nova-based code in place (do NOT delete it) with a comment explaining the rate-limit problem that motivated the move.

WHY: the current Nova path (StatementSuggestionsService + BedrockClient.suggest) has two problems in production: (1) it asks the model to return ids/text and often comes back empty or unmappable; (2) it runs via the `eu.` cross-region inference profile, whose quota "Cross-region model inference requests per minute for Amazon Nova Lite" is capped at 20/min and is NOT adjustable, so per-row calls hit ThrottlingException (429). JEV's `Choice` primitive instead SELECTS one option from a fixed set and returns the chosen key verbatim plus a calibrated confidence — removing the empty-result failures and the id-echo/name-matching fragility — and uses its own (more generous) quota.

JEV API (already have a key): `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`, header `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, JSON body:
{ "model":"jev-latest", "state":"<the transaction text>", "questions": { "<name>": { "type":"choice", "instructions":"<what to decide>", "criteria": { "<optionKey>":"<option description>", ... } } } }
Response: { "answers": { "<name>": { "type":"choice", "choice":"<the chosen optionKey>", "confidence":<0..1>, "probabilities": {..} } }, "usage": { "input_tokens":N } }. A Choice accepts up to 255 options and always returns one of the criteria keys.

BUILD:

1. JEV client (in server .../apis), mirroring the existing external-API pattern (ReCaptchaApi uses Play `WSClient` + play-json; RealBedrockClient/MockBedrockClient show the Real/Mock split):
   - `JevConfig` read from Configuration like BedrockConfig: api key from env `JEV_API_KEY`, base url (default `https://api.typesafe.ai`), model alias (default `jev-latest`), and a `mode` (mock|real) defaulting to mock so tests and uninitialised envs never call JEV.
   - `JevClient` trait with a `RealJevClient` (injects `WSClient`, POSTs the body above with Bearer auth, parses the response, fails loud on non-2xx or unparseable, and surfaces HTTP 429 as a distinct retryable error) and a `MockJevClient` for tests. Bind Real/Mock by `mode` in ServicesModule exactly like `bedrockClient`.
   - A method like `choose(state: String, questionName: String, instructions: String, criteria: Map[String, String]): Future[JevChoice]` where `JevChoice(choice: String, confidence: BigDecimal, probabilities: Map[String, BigDecimal])`.

2. A JEV-based suggestions engine that produces the same `AiSuggestions` output as the Nova one. Reuse — do NOT reimplement or regress — the behaviour added in PR #11: the deterministic history tier (normalized description -> the user's prior category), skipping rule-matched rows via the shared rule resolver, dedup so only DISTINCT descriptions are resolved, and failing loud when there are rows to resolve but the user's categories are empty. Only novel distinct descriptions go to JEV. For each such description:
   - Category: one JEV `Choice`. Key the `criteria` by the category id (value = category name plus its few-shot example descriptions). JEV returns the chosen key, i.e. the category id, so it maps straight back with NO name matching — this also sidesteps the real `Super`/`Súper` duplicate. State = the row description (optionally include the amount).
   - Merchant (KEEP this step): if a category was chosen and it has merchants, a second JEV `Choice` whose `criteria` are that category's merchants keyed by merchant id (value = merchant name) PLUS an explicit `"none"` option; `"none"` (or a key that isn't a merchant) means no merchant. The chosen merchant's category stays authoritative over the predicted one, as today.
   - Apply each distinct description's result to all rows sharing that description.
   - The stored `AiSuggestions.RowSuggestion` shape is unchanged (rowId, categoryId, merchantId) — do NOT add a confidence column; confidence is available from JEV for future gating but is not persisted now.

3. Wire `ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction` to the JEV engine (bind it in DI). Everything else about the job stays: single atomic write, Done/Failed status, re-raise on failure so the executor retries.

4. KEEP the Nova code. Do not delete `StatementSuggestionsService` (Nova), `BedrockClient.suggest`, or its prompt/parse helpers. Leave them compiling (an unwired public class is fine; make sure nothing becomes an unused-private `-Werror` failure). Add a clear comment on the Nova suggestions service stating: it was the prior engine; on the `eu.` cross-region profile it is throttled by the non-adjustable 20 req/min "Cross-region model inference requests per minute for Amazon Nova Lite" quota (ThrottlingException 429 on per-row calls); JEV is now the active engine; kept for reference/fallback.

5. RATE-LIMIT COMMENT: we are deliberately NOT adding an app-level rate limiter in this change. Add a short comment (near the JEV client or the suggestions config) noting that Nova hit the 20 req/min cross-region cap, that JEV has its own (separate, more generous) request limit and can also return 429, and that if JEV throttling appears the planned next step is a Postgres single-row "spacing" rate limiter (one row per resource, atomic upsert bumping a `next_available_at` timestamp) — not implemented yet. Keep a light backoff on JEV 429 (transient; the background job already retries).

6. Config: add the `jev { ... }` block to application.conf following the `bedrock`/`bda` blocks (env overrides, mock default). Log the loaded JEV mode like the others, but NEVER log the api key.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Follow docs/guide (antipatterns, backend, data-infra, testing, ci-checklist).
- User-scoped DB access; no silent defaults (fail loud); log the work with the userId in scope (per the coding-patterns reviewer rule); use Chimney for case-class mapping; prefer enums over stringly-typed values; never drop a Future.
- Surgical: do NOT change the draft->confirm flow, the AiSuggestions DB column/model, the regenerate endpoint, or the review-page UI.
- Tests: `MockJevClient`; the JEV suggestions engine (history-first so a row with history skips JEV; dedup so duplicate descriptions cause one call; category choice mapped back to its id; merchant choice including the `none` case; categories-empty-with-rows fails loud); JevConfig parsing. Keep the existing Nova StatementSuggestionsService tests passing.

resultJson.description:
Move the bank-statement AI category/merchant suggestions off Amazon Nova Lite (Bedrock) and onto TypeSafe JEV's "System One" `Choice` primitive. The Nova path has two problems in production. First, it asks the model to write a category or merchant name, which often comes back empty or doesn't map to exactly one candidate (for example the real `Super`/`Súper` duplicate). Second, it runs through the `eu.` cross-region inference profile, whose quota "Cross-region model inference requests per minute for Amazon Nova Lite" is capped at 20/min and can't be raised, so per-row calls get ThrottlingException (429). JEV's `Choice` picks one key from a fixed `criteria` map and returns that key exactly, with a confidence score. If we key the criteria by category id and merchant id, the answer maps straight back to an id with no name matching, and JEV has its own, separate quota.

The new engine (`JevStatementSuggestionsService`) returns the same `AiSuggestions` value as the Nova `StatementSuggestionsService` and reuses the selection logic from PR #11 instead of reimplementing it: skip credits and rule-matched rows (shared `RowRuleVerdict`), apply the deterministic history tier first, and fail loudly when there are rows to resolve but the user has no categories. It also adds something new: deduplication. Only distinct novel descriptions go to JEV, each description is resolved once (a category Choice, then a merchant Choice with an explicit `"none"` option when that category has merchants), and the result is applied to every row with that description. If a merchant is chosen, its category overrides the predicted one, as today. Confidence is logged but not stored. The `AiSuggestions` DB column and model, the draft→confirm flow, the regenerate endpoint and the review UI do not change.

`ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction` switches to the JEV engine. It keeps the single atomic write, the Done/Failed status, and re-raising so the background executor retries. The Nova code (`StatementSuggestionsService`, `BedrockClient.suggest`, its prompt and parse helpers, and its spec) stays and keeps compiling. It gets a comment explaining the 20 req/min cross-region throttling that motivated the move. We are deliberately not adding an app-level rate limiter. `RealJevClient` does a short backoff on 429, and a comment records the planned next step if JEV throttling shows up: a Postgres single-row "spacing" limiter, one row per resource, with an atomic upsert bumping `next_available_at`.

tasks.title: Add JevConfig, the `jev { }` application.conf block and its ConfigModule provider
tasks.description: Create `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/config/JevConfig.scala`: `case class JevConfig(apiKey: JevApiKey, baseUrl: String, model: String, mode: JevConfig.Mode)` with `object JevConfig { sealed trait Mode; case object Mock extends Mode; case object Real extends Mode; def apply(config: Configuration): JevConfig }`. Parse mode the same way as BedrockConfig/BdaConfig ("mock"/"real", anything else throws `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown jev.mode '...'; expected 'mock' or 'real'")`). Add `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/models/JevApiKey.scala` (`case class JevApiKey(string: String) extends SecretValue(string)` plus a `ConfigLoader`, copying `AWSSecretAccessKey`). Override `JevConfig.toString` so it shows only mode, baseUrl and model, never the key. In `ConfigModule` add `@Provides @Singleton def jevConfig(global: Configuration): JevConfig` reading `global.get[Configuration]("jev")` and logging `Config loaded: jev.mode=..., baseUrl=..., model=...` (no key). In `server/src/main/resources/application.conf`, add a `jev { }` block right after `bda { }`, written like `bedrock`/`bda`: `mode = "mock"` / `${?JEV_MODE}` (with a comment saying mock never calls JEV and is safe for tests and uninitialised envs), `apiKey = "REPLACE_ME"` / `${?JEV_API_KEY}`, `baseUrl = "https://api.typesafe.ai"` / `${?JEV_BASE_URL}`, `model = "jev-latest"` / `${?JEV_MODEL}`. Add a short comment there saying JEV runs the statement category/merchant suggestions, replacing Nova Lite, which hit the non-adjustable 20 req/min cross-region quota. Tests: new `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/config/JevConfigSpec.scala` (AnyWordSpec, built from `Configuration(ConfigFactory.parseString(...))`): parses mock and real with all fields, throws on an unknown mode, and `toString` does not contain the api key. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *JevConfigSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Add JevClient trait with RealJevClient (WSClient, 429 backoff) and MockJevClient, bound by mode in ServicesModule
tasks.description: In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/`, add `JevClient.scala` with `trait JevClient { def choose(state: String, questionName: String, instructions: String, criteria: Map[String, String]): Future[JevChoice] }`, `case class JevChoice(choice: String, confidence: BigDecimal, probabilities: Map[String, BigDecimal])` and `class JevRateLimitedException(message: String) extends RuntimeException(message)` (the distinct retryable 429 error). `RealJevClient(config: JevConfig, ws: WSClient, actorSystem: ActorSystem)(implicit ec: ExecutionContext)` sends `POST ${config.baseUrl}/v1/systemone` with headers `Authorization: Bearer ${config.apiKey.string}` and `Content-Type: application/json`, and body `{model: config.model, state, questions: {questionName: {type: "choice", instructions, criteria}}}` built with play-json and sent via `play.api.libs.ws.JsonBodyWritables`. Handle responses like this: on 2xx, parse `answers.<questionName>` and require `type == "choice"`, a string `choice` that is one of the `criteria` keys, a numeric `confidence` and a `probabilities` object; otherwise fail with a RuntimeException that includes the status and response body (never the key). On 429, retry lightly, at most 2 retries with about 1s then 2s delay using `org.apache.pekko.pattern.after(delay, actorSystem.scheduler)` as `RealBdaClient` does, then fail with `JevRateLimitedException`. Any other non-2xx fails with a RuntimeException that includes the status and body. Put a scaladoc comment on RealJevClient covering: Nova hit the 20 req/min "Cross-region model inference requests per minute for Amazon Nova Lite" cap; JEV has its own, separate and more generous request limit but can also return 429; we deliberately don't add an app-level limiter (the light backoff here plus the background job's retry are enough for now); if JEV throttling appears, the planned next step is a Postgres single-row "spacing" rate limiter (one row per resource, atomic upsert bumping `next_available_at`), not implemented yet. `MockJevClient` must be stateless, with no mutable collections (Wart.MutableDataStructures is enforced on main code). It always succeeds deterministically: it picks `"none"` if that key is in `criteria`, otherwise the smallest key, with confidence 0 and an empty probabilities map. Document that mock-mode suggestions are placeholder picks. In `ServicesModule`, add `@Provides @Singleton def jevClient(config: JevConfig, ws: WSClient, actorSystem: ActorSystem, ec: ExecutionContext): JevClient` matching `config.mode` exactly like `bedrockClient`. Tests: `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/RealJevClientSpec.scala` using Mockito WSClient/WSRequest/WSResponse as in `ReCaptchaApiSpec` (mock `url`, `addHttpHeaders`, `post[JsValue]`, `status`, `json`, `body`), with a real `ActorSystem` that is terminated in `afterAll` and a patience of about 10s. Cover: sends the expected JSON body and Bearer header (ArgumentCaptor); parses choice, confidence and probabilities; fails on non-2xx with the status in the message; fails on an unparseable body or a choice not in criteria; a 429 followed by 200 succeeds; persistent 429 fails with `JevRateLimitedException`. Add `MockJevClientSpec`: chooses `none` when offered, otherwise a deterministic key from criteria. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *RealJevClientSpec *MockJevClientSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Add JevStatementSuggestionsService reusing the PR #11 selection/history helpers, with dedup and category+merchant Choices
tasks.description: Create `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/JevStatementSuggestionsService.scala`: `class JevStatementSuggestionsService @Inject() (jevClient: JevClient)(implicit ec: ExecutionContext)` with the same signature as the Nova service: `def resolve(userId: UUID, statementId: UUID, modelId: String, rows: List[BankStatementRow], rules: List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule], merchants: List[Merchant], categories: List[Category], examples: List[(UUID, String)], history: Map[String, UUID]): Future[AiSuggestions]`. Reuse instead of reimplementing: widen `RowSelection`, `selectRowsToResolve` and `historyCategories` in `object StatementSuggestionsService` from `private` to `private[services]` (`finalSuggestion` already is) and call them. Logic: select the rows; if nothing is left, return `AiSuggestions(Done, modelId, Nil)` with no JEV call; if rows remain and `categories.isEmpty`, log an error with the userId and `Future.failed(RuntimeException("User $userId has no categories to suggest for statement $statementId"))`, using the same message as Nova because the action spec asserts on "no categories". Otherwise apply the history hits first. Group the remaining rows by dedup key `ImportRuleMatcher.normalize(description)`; when the normalized key is empty, use the whitespace-collapsed raw description so unrelated junk rows aren't merged. Resolve each distinct key sequentially (foldLeft over Futures, as Nova does, so load stays predictable) using the first row's whitespace-collapsed description as `state`, without the amount so dedup holds. Category step: `jevClient.choose(state, "category", <instructions: pick the user's expense category this bank transaction belongs to>, categories.map(c => c.id.toString -> <name plus up to the examples for c.id, e.g. "Groceries. Examples: X; Y">).toMap)`, then map the choice back with `categories.find(_.id.toString == choice)` and fail loudly if it isn't found. If there are more than 255 categories, fail loudly before calling. Merchant step: when the category has candidates (`merchants.filter(_.categoryId.contains(category.id))`), call `choose(state, "merchant", <instructions mentioning the category name and that "none" means no listed merchant fits>, candidates.map(m => m.id.toString -> m.name).toMap + ("none" -> "No listed merchant fits this transaction"))`. `"none"` or a non-merchant key gives no merchant; fail loudly if there are more than 254 candidates. Build the result with `StatementSuggestionsService.finalSuggestion(row.id, Some(category.id), merchantId, merchants)` for every row sharing the key, so the merchant's category stays authoritative. Return the rows in the original `toResolve` order. Logging (always with `userId`): counts of rows, history hits, distinct descriptions sent to JEV and JEV calls; one line per resolved description with category and merchant names plus the JEV confidence (not persisted). Never drop a Future. Tests: new `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/services/JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec.scala`, modelled on `StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec` (same row/category/merchant builders), with a test-only `StubJevClient` that records `(state, questionName, criteria)` calls (mutable ListBuffer is fine in tests) and answers via a function. Cover: rule-matched and credit rows are never sent; a history hit skips JEV; duplicate descriptions (including ones that differ only in case or punctuation) cause one category call and all rows get the result; category criteria are keyed by category id and the chosen id maps back (including two categories named `Super`/`Súper`); merchant criteria are the predicted category's merchants keyed by id plus `none`; a chosen merchant is set and its category overrides; `none` keeps the predicted category with no merchant; a category without merchants skips the merchant call; a client failure propagates; no rows gives Done/Nil with no calls; rows without categories fail with the userId in the message and no calls. Leave `StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec` unchanged and passing. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec *StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Wire ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction to the JEV engine and annotate the Nova service as the retired engine
tasks.description: In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.scala`, replace the injected `StatementSuggestionsService` and `BedrockConfig` with `JevStatementSuggestionsService` and `JevConfig`, and use `jevConfig.model` as `modelId`, for both the Done result and the Failed record. Nothing else changes: same repository loads (rows, importRules → `transformInto[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]` via Chimney, merchants, categories, `categorizedRowExamples(userId, ExamplesPerCategory)`, `categoryHistory(userId)`), a single `setAiSuggestions` write, a Failed write on error, and re-raising the original cause. Add `userId=${statement.userId}` to the store and failure log lines (coding-patterns rule). Guice binding: the engine is a concrete `@Inject` class (JIT-bound) and `JevClient` is already provided by ServicesModule, so no extra module code is needed unless it fails to resolve. Don't touch `RegenerateAiSuggestionsAction`: it still writes Pending with `bedrockConfig.suggestionsModelId`, which the job overwrites. On `StatementSuggestionsService` (Nova), add a scaladoc paragraph saying it was the prior suggestions engine; on the `eu.` cross-region inference profile it is throttled by the non-adjustable 20 req/min "Cross-region model inference requests per minute for Amazon Nova Lite" quota (ThrottlingException 429 on per-row calls); `JevStatementSuggestionsService` is now the active engine; it's kept, unwired, for reference and fallback. Optionally add a one-line pointer on `BedrockClient.suggest`. Delete nothing. Tests: update `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec.scala` to build the action with `new JevStatementSuggestionsService(stubJevClient)` and a test `JevConfig(JevApiKey("test"), "https://example.invalid", "test-jev-model", JevConfig.Mock)`. Replace `StubBedrockClient` with a stub JevClient answering by `(state, questionName, criteria)`: for category, return the key whose criterion text holds the matching category name; for merchant, return the merchant id key. Keep the existing scenarios: Done for the debit rows no rule handles, with category and merchant ids; history row not sent to JEV (fail if its description arrives as state); client failure stores `AiSuggestions(Failed, "test-jev-model", Nil)` and fails; no categories stores Failed and the message contains "no categories"; missing statement fails. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec *StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec *JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- `server/` (Play, Scala 3.8.3): controllers → actions → repositories/services. External APIs live in `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/`, config wrappers in `.../config/`, DI in `.../modules/{ConfigModule,ServicesModule}.scala`, pure-ish engines in `.../services/`.
- `lib/api/shared/`: `net.wiringbits.api.models.bankstatements.{AiSuggestions, AiSuggestionsStatus}` (`AiSuggestions(status, model: String, rows: List[AiSuggestions.RowSuggestion])`, `RowSuggestion(rowId: UUID, categoryId: Option[UUID], merchantId: Option[UUID])`; statuses Pending/Done/Failed) and `net.wiringbits.api.utils.{ImportRuleMatcher, RowRuleVerdict}`. `ImportRuleMatcher.normalize(s)` lowercases and strips accents, punctuation and spaces (\"corner-shop #42\" → \"cornershop42\"). Do NOT change these.

KEY FILES
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala`: the Nova engine (keep it). The companion holds `private case class RowSelection(toResolve, creditsSkipped, ruleSkipped)`, `private def selectRowsToResolve(rows, rules): RowSelection` (debits with `RowRuleVerdict.verdict(rules, desc) == RowRuleVerdict.NoRule`), `private def historyCategories(rows, history, categories): Map[rowId, categoryId]` (drops categories not among the loaded ones), `private[services] def finalSuggestion(rowId, predictedCategoryId, chosenMerchantId, merchants): RowSuggestion` (the merchant's category wins), `matchByName`, the prompts, `parseAnswer`. The Nova engine does NOT dedup; dedup is new in the JEV engine. To reuse the helpers from the JEV engine (same package `net.wiringbits.services`), widen `private` → `private[services]`; that's the only change Nova needs besides the comment. Its current \"no categories\" error: `RuntimeException(s\"User $userId has no categories to suggest for statement $statementId\")`.
- `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/services/StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec.scala`: the Nova spec; must keep passing untouched. A good template for builders: `row(description, amount = -10)` builds `BankStatementRow(id, bankStatementId, index, date, amount, description, manuallyEdited, confirmedAt, expenseId, refundId, ignoredAt, txnType = \"purchase\", createdAt, updatedAt)`; `Category(UUID, userId, name, now, now)`; `Merchant(UUID, userId, name, None, categoryId: Option[UUID], None, reviewed = true, now, now)`; `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule(id, ImportRuleAction.Ignore|SetMerchant, pattern, merchantId)`; StubBedrockClient uses a mutable ListBuffer (OK in tests only).
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.scala`: the background job (called from `tasks/BackgroundJobsExecutorTask.scala` with a bankStatementId). It loads `bankStatementRepository.findInternal(id)`, then `findRows(statement.id)`, `importRuleRepository.all(userId)`, `merchantsRepository.all(userId)`, `categoriesRepository.all(userId)`, `bankStatementRepository.categorizedRowExamples(userId, 3)`, `categoryHistory(userId): Future[Map[String, UUID]]`, maps rules with Chimney `transformInto[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]`, calls `suggestionsService.resolve(...)`, `setAiSuggestions(statement.id, statement.userId, suggestions, clock.instant())`, and on NonFatal stores `AiSuggestions(Failed, modelId, Nil)` and re-raises. Constructor `(...)(implicit ec, clock: Clock)`; tests construct it with `(using executionContext, Clock.systemUTC())`.
- `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec.scala`: extends `RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils`, uses `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`, seeds via `createUser/createCategory/createMerchant/createImportRule/createDocument/createStatement(stmt, sampleStatementMetadata, rows)`; history via an expense + `ExpenseCategorySplit` + `setRowExpenseIdForUser`.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/RegenerateAiSuggestionsAction.scala`: writes Pending with `bedrockConfig.suggestionsModelId`. Do NOT touch it (constraint); the job's Done/Failed write overwrites the model label.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/{BedrockClient,RealBedrockClient,MockBedrockClient}.scala`: the Real/Mock pattern; `suggest(prompt)` must stay.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/ReCaptchaApi.scala`: the WSClient + play-json pattern (`ws.url(...).post(...)`, `response.json`). Test pattern in `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/ReCaptchaApiSpec.scala` (Mockito `mock[WSClient]`, `when(request.post[String](anyString())(using any[BodyWritable[String]]()))`). For JsValue bodies use `play.api.libs.ws.JsonBodyWritables.*` and mock `post[JsValue]`.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/RealBdaClient.scala`: backoff via `import org.apache.pekko.pattern.after; after(delay, actorSystem.scheduler)(future)`; ActorSystem is injected through ServicesModule (`bdaClient(config, awsConfig, actorSystem: ActorSystem, ec)`).
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/config/{BedrockConfig,BdaConfig}.scala`: config pattern: `case class X(...); object X { sealed trait Mode; case object Mock extends Mode; case object Real extends Mode; def apply(config: Configuration): X }`, mode parsed from \"mock\"/\"real\" with an IllegalArgumentException otherwise. Secrets: `net.wiringbits.models.SecretValue` (masked toString), e.g. `AWSSecretAccessKey(string)` with a `ConfigLoader`.
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/modules/ConfigModule.scala`: `@Provides @Singleton def xConfig(global: Configuration) = X(global.get[Configuration](\"x\"))` and logs `Config loaded: ...` (bda logs only the mode). `ServicesModule.scala`: `@Provides @Singleton def bedrockClient(config, ec) = config.mode match { case Mock => new MockBedrockClient(); case Real => new RealBedrockClient(config)(using ec) }`.
- `server/src/main/resources/application.conf`: `bedrock { }` (around lines 169-207, including the Nova Lite `suggestionsModelId = \"eu.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0\"`), then `bda { }` (209-229), then `aws { }`. The `jev { }` block goes after `bda`. There is no separate test application.conf; tests run with the defaults (mock mode).

CONVENTIONS / GOTCHAS
- `CI=true` turns on `-Werror`. Wartremover on MAIN code: MutableDataStructures, Null, OptionPartial, Return, TryPartial, IsInstanceOf. So MockJevClient must be stateless; no `.get` on Option, no null, no `return`.
- Keeping the Nova service compiling and unwired is fine because it's a public class. Widening its helpers to `private[services]` doesn't cause unused warnings; only remove imports that your own change leaves unused (e.g. `BedrockConfig` in the action once it's replaced; BedrockConfig is still used elsewhere).
- Coding-patterns reviewer (`.orca/reviewers/coding-patterns.md`): Chimney for case-class mapping; never drop a Future; no silent defaults (fail with a RuntimeException naming what was missing or unexpected); prefer sealed trait/enum over strings for fixed sets (Mode); every log about a user's data includes `userId=$userId` (or `User $userId ...` as the Nova service does); never log the JEV api key (keep it out of toString and error messages).
- Errors: plain `RuntimeException` (no typed hierarchy, AP-BE-01). The only distinct type is the new `JevRateLimitedException` for 429.
- Tests: ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec` + `Matchers` (must), `ScalaFutures` `.futureValue` / `.failed.futureValue`. `should` subjects name the method or behaviour, never the class (RULE-TE-001). Spec paths mirror source paths. Use Mockito only for WSClient-level external boundaries.
- Verify per task with targeted `sbt \"testOnly *XSpec\"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`; do NOT run the full `sbt test`. DB-backed specs (RepositorySpec) need Docker/testcontainers.
- JEV API: `POST {baseUrl}/v1/systemone`, `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Body `{\"model\":\"jev-latest\",\"state\":\"...\",\"questions\":{\"<name>\":{\"type\":\"choice\",\"instructions\":\"...\",\"criteria\":{\"<key>\":\"<desc>\"}}}}`. Response `{\"answers\":{\"<name>\":{\"type\":\"choice\",\"choice\":\"<key>\",\"confidence\":0..1,\"probabilities\":{...}}},\"usage\":{\"input_tokens\":N}}`. At most 255 options per Choice, and it always returns one of the criteria keys. Criteria keys for categories and merchants are `UUID.toString`; the merchant question also offers the literal key `\"none\"`.
- Out of scope: the AiSuggestions DB column/model, the draft→confirm flow, the regenerate endpoint, the review-page UI, storing confidence, and an app-level rate limiter.
